sources.claim: Investigative feature (12 January 2018) on the plight of transgender women in French prisons: incarcerated on the basis of legal gender status, most trans women housed in all-male facilities because placement follows the sex on the ID document (Article D248 of the criminal procedure code separates men and women only); first-person accounts (a trans woman held in a northern correctional facility in 2014 shouted at by other detainees; another foreign trans woman detained after a publicised 2016 Paris protest trial); the controller-general of places of deprivation of liberty says transgender detainees - the majority of whom are women - are the group that 'suffers the most' in prison.

Opinion of 25 May 2021 of the controller-general of places of deprivation of liberty (unofficial English translation) on the treatment of transgender persons in places of deprivation of liberty: serious violations of fundamental rights persist across all detention settings, based on some forty referrals since 2010, interviews with trans associations and European experts, observations from the interior, justice and health ministries, and on-site/document inspections; recommendations extend to intersex and non-binary persons; follows an initial 2010 opinion on transsexual prisoners.

sources.claim: BuzzFeed News feature (12 Jan 2018), 'The Plight Of Trans Women In Prison': transgender women incarcerated in France on the basis of their legal gender fall into a legal grey area and are punished for far more than their alleged crimes - first-person accounts of placement in an all-male facility (a three-day stay in Lille's men's prison in 2014, with detainee and staff hostility; an Argentinian trans woman's story of incarceration); Article D248 of the criminal procedure code assigns detainees by the sex on their ID; the controller-general of places of deprivation of liberty says transgender detainees are the group that 'suffers the most' in prison; also covers the well-publicised case of a US trans woman detained in poor conditions after a 2016 Paris protest case.

Opinion of 25 May 2021 of the Contrôleur général des lieux de privation de liberté (CGLPL), unofficial English translation: official inspectorate opinion on the treatment of transgender persons in ALL places of deprivation of liberty; built on about forty referrals received since 2010, interviews with trans associations and European experts, and five on-site inspections (Fleury-Mérogis men's and women's prisons, Caen, Saint-Martin-de-Ré, Toulouse-Seysses and the Toulouse central police station - eight trans women and one trans man interviewed); finds persistent serious violations of fundamental rights of trans detainees, isolation and overcrowding risks; recommends that the 2016 depathologising law (no more surgery requirement for civil-status change) be translated into prison regulations; explicitly extends to intersex and non-binary people.
